title: How do I test food/soil for heavy metals at home?

grade.title: No qualifying human study in this corpus
grade.outcome: An at-home food or soil metal test
grade.basis: No qualifying method-validation study was located in this corpus.

answerHtml: This corpus does not contain a validated at-home method for measuring metals in food or soil, and it does not contain performance data for a consumer kit. No detection limit, false-result rate, or pass-fail number is stated, because none was verified. Laboratory methods such as ICP-MS are the methods named by FDA for cobalt and chromium in blood, which is a different sample.

sections.heading: What is not available
sections.html: Questions about testing water, soil, and food at home are in the question set. The saved sources do not evaluate a home kit. Naming a product would go beyond those sources. Certified laboratory testing is a different activity from a home test, and this page does not list laboratories.

sources.text: FDA metal-ion testing methods for cobalt and chromium in whole blood (a clinical specimen, not food or soil)

heavyMetalIndexHtml: Heavy Metal Index: ICP-MS testing. This Heavy Metal Index URL returned HTTP 200 on 15 October 2026. Figures on this page are not copied from that index. They come from the sources named above.
buyHtml:
The Heavy Metal Tested and Certified public register listed no licensees on 15 October 2026. That page reported 0 certified brands and 0 certified products, and it stated that no brand has completed the three-lot baseline. A specimen layout on the register is an illustration, not a licensee. This page does not name or rank any brand.

The program states that certification is a measurement of a product against a published limit, not a statement that the product is safe. If a licensee is later listed for this category, it will be on the register.
